what_its_for: Armodafinil helps you stay awake if you have certain sleep disorders. It is used for narcolepsy (a condition that causes you to fall asleep suddenly during the day), obstructive sleep apnea (where breathing stops during sleep and causes daytime sleepiness), and shift work sleep disorder (trouble staying awake during your work shift). It does NOT cure these conditions or replace the need for good sleep.
how_to_take: Take armodafinil by mouth, with or without food. Food may slow how quickly it works but will not affect how well it works. Swallow the tablet whole. Take it at the same time each day. For narcolepsy or sleep apnea, take it in the morning. For shift work disorder, take it about 1 hour before your work shift begins. Do not crush, split, or chew the tablet unless your doctor or pharmacist says it is okay.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 150 mg to 250 mg once a day in the morning (for narcolepsy or sleep apnea) or 150 mg taken about 1 hour before your work shift (for shift work disorder). Your doctor will decide the right dose for you. Do not take more than prescribed. Taking higher doses does not make it work better and increases your risk of side effects.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — BUT only if it is still early enough in your day that it will not keep you awake when you need to sleep. If it is already close to your bedtime or your next sleep time, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at once to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store armodafinil at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the medication in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medication down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking armodafinil — it can increase dizziness and may make your condition worse. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing any activity that requires you to be fully alert until you know how this medication affects you. Avoid taking armodafinil late in the day or close to your sleep time, as it can cause insomnia (trouble sleeping). If you use hormonal birth control (pills, patches, rings, implants, or injections), armodafinil may make them less effective — use a backup method of birth control (such as condoms) during treatment and for 1 month after stopping. Avoid caffeine in large amounts as it may increase side effects like nervousness or rapid heartbeat.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency medical help if you notice: a skin rash, hives, blisters, or peeling skin (this could be a sign of a rare but serious reaction); swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat; trouble breathing or swallowing; fever, sore throat, or mouth sores; chest pain or irregular heartbeat; mental or mood changes such as anxiety, aggression, confusion, hallucinations, or thoughts of self-harm; or signs of an allergic reaction. Also call your doctor if you develop depression, feel unusually agitated, or notice any new or worsening mental health symptoms.
when_it_works: Armodafinil usually starts working within 1 to 2 hours after you take it. Most people notice they feel more awake and alert within the first few days of starting treatment. It works best when taken consistently at the same time every day. Keep taking it even if you feel well — do not stop without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older): Your doctor may start you on a lower dose because your body may process this drug more slowly, increasing the risk of side effects. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease. If your liver is not working well, your doctor may lower your dose. Pregnancy: It is not known if armodafinil is safe during pregnancy. Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: It is not known if armodafinil passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while taking this medication. Children: Armodafinil is not approved for use in children and should not be given to anyone under 17 years of age.
